first_impression.reaction: My assistant sent it because the Seychelles is on our list next to Mauritius. The first screen is calm. It answers the legal question in two words and doesn't sell. No prices, no 'affordable'. It's still a paperwork guide for two Australians doing it themselves, but this time there's a section that sounds like it knows families like mine exist. Her summary would be 'clear on the legal order, and it asks the right privacy questions of the resort'. I read the takeaways, the civil ceremony idea, the resort section and the close.

journey.reaction: Good. No hedging, no gushing. That's the tone I want from an adviser.

journey.quote: Getting married in Seychelles is open to two Australians, because anyone aged 18 or over may marry under Seychelles law.
journey.reaction: We're between Dubai, Sydney and London. The whole page assumes two Australian passports. My assistant would have to work out what applies to us.

journey.quote: Some couples keep the civil marriage small and quiet with only their witnesses, then gather everyone on the sand in the late afternoon for the vows they have written.
journey.reaction: This is how I'd want it. The legal part private, with family only and no phones, and the large ceremony later.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Look at your guests' routes as well as your own, particularly anyone pairing the wedding with time on the African mainland.
journey.reaction: Someone thinking about guests flying in from several continents. That matters with 300 people.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Keep your passports in good order and well clear of expiry, because a replacement cannot be arranged on the islands.
journey.reaction: The reason is useful. 'Keep your passports in good order' is the kind of thing you tell a first-time traveller. My assistant handles this.

journey.section: Ceremonies on the beach, at your resort or on another island
journey.quote: For a high-profile family or a guest list with privacy needs, ask the resort:
journey.reaction: Finally. It doesn't flatter me, it just acknowledges that some clients need more than a pretty beach. This is the line my assistant would highlight.

journey.section: Ceremonies on the beach, at your resort or on another island
journey.quote: Security. Who controls access to the ceremony area, and how are drones and outside photographers handled?
journey.reaction: Drones and outside photographers are exactly what keeps me up at night. Whoever wrote this has thought about leaks. I'd add how the venue's security works with our own team, but this is close.

journey.section: Ceremonies on the beach, at your resort or on another island
journey.quote: Exclusive use. Can you take the whole property, or the ceremony space alone, and for how many hours?
journey.reaction: Right question, but 'for how many hours' is small thinking. I'm asking about three days, not an afternoon.

journey.section: Ceremonies on the beach, at your resort or on another island
journey.quote: People in the Seychelles are usually very traditional, so avoid public displays of affection, especially in rural or traditional places.
journey.reaction: Cultural awareness without lecturing. Our families would appreciate knowing this, and it's another reason for a private setting.

journey.section: Ceremonies on the beach, at your resort or on another island
journey.quote: If a resort presents a wedding package, ask whether it covers the civil formalities, the officer's attendance and the certificate errands after the wedding, and ask for that list in writing.
journey.reaction: Only once this time and it's aimed at the resort, so it doesn't bother me much. We wouldn't be buying a package either way.

journey.section: When to marry in the Seychelles
journey.quote: Pack insect repellent, choose insect-proof accommodation and see your doctor about health risks and vaccines before you go.
journey.reaction: Packing tips. This is for couples who've never hosted anything. Skip.

journey.quote: Many couples do exactly that, with a long lunch at home for the friends who could not make the flight.
journey.reaction: Pleasant, but it assumes a small wedding with friends left behind. Ours would be the other way round.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans your venue, travel, vendors and payments as one point of contact from start to finish, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: One point of contact suits me, because fewer people means fewer leaks. 'Inclusions' still sounds a little like a package.

journey.section: Plan your Seychelles wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Fee agreed in writing is right for my family office. AUD and 'your time zone' assume I'm sitting in Sydney.

unanswered_questions: Have you planned a Seychelles wedding for 200 to 400 guests, and can you show me one discreetly? (deferred business detail)
How is the Wedded Advisor fee worked out, and do you earn commission from the resorts you book? (deferred business detail)
Who would actually be on the ground in the Seychelles for us during the wedding week? (deferred business detail)
Do you arrange private transfers, inter-island flights or boats, and airport handling for us and our guests? (deferred business detail)
What access or perks come with booking through you, such as Wedded Privileges? (deferred business detail)
Would you handle the Civil Status office arrangements, the apostilles and the certificate errands for us, or are we expected to do them ourselves? (deferred business detail)
Can a private island or whole resort be taken for several days, with our own security working alongside the venue's?
Does the process differ if one of us is not Australian, or if our witnesses hold other passports?
How do you handle confidentiality: NDAs, guest lists, no social media?
Can I work through my assistant or family office, and can you quote in another currency?

turn_offs_found.quote: Pack insect repellent, choose insect-proof accommodation and see your doctor about health risks and vaccines before you go.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explaining. Packing advice makes the page read as written for first-timers, not for someone hiring a premium planner.

turn_offs_found.quote: Keep your passports in good order and well clear of expiry, because a replacement cannot be arranged on the islands.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explaining. The fact about no replacement is enough; the instruction is patronising.

turn_offs_found.quote: If a resort presents a wedding package, ask whether it covers the civil formalities, the officer's attendance and the certificate errands after the wedding, and ask for that list in writing.
turn_offs_found.why: Package language. Mild here because it's aimed at the resort, but it still frames the wedding as a standard product.

would_share_with: My assistant would keep the privacy and security questions for the resort and the private civil ceremony idea in the planning file. Nobody else.

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [start a conversation with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=getting-married-in-seychelles&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: I don't enquire through a public link on a blog post. The resort questions show you understand discretion, which is more than most, but I'd still want a private introduction and some sign you've done this at our size.

top_3_changes: In the privacy list, extend the exclusive-use question beyond hours (for example 'for how many hours or days') and add whether the venue's security can work alongside a private security team. Keep it as a question to ask, not a claim about Wedded Wonderland.

Trim the over-explaining: cut 'Pack insect repellent, choose insect-proof accommodation' down to the health fact and the doctor visit, and drop 'Keep your passports in good order' in favour of the fact that a replacement cannot be arranged on the islands.
Soften the small-wedding assumption in 'Many couples do exactly that, with a long lunch at home for the friends who could not make the flight.' so it doesn't presume a short guest list.
